weekly_marks.summary: **Week 1 summary (2026-02-23 → 2026-02-27):** P&L flat at $0.00 / 0.00% on a $10k book — no fills, no positions, 100% cash. Onboarded Friday afternoon into a bearish SPY outside-reversal bar (693→689 on rising volume), which is exactly the tape where the seed playbook says don't initiate. Best decisions: respecting Friday-PM no-add, leading with macro context, and pre-scripting a Monday trigger. Misses: didn't read VIX, didn't pull histories on watchlist names for level-prep, and defined a trigger without a paired invalidation level. Playbook now mandates VIX in every macro check, requires trigger + invalidation on every plan, and codifies the stop ladder (−4% hard / BE at +3% / −5% trail at +6% / −8% at +10%). Monday plan: SPY 8% tranche if 682 holds in the first 30 minutes with stop at 678; otherwise stay flat and let the range resolve.

**Week 2 summary for operator:** Closed −$51.86 / −0.52% on the $10k book — a small red week, mandate-violating in the strictest "green every week" reading but well within capital-preservation tolerance. We took three fills (SPY starter 3/2, SPY add + META starter 3/4) and cut SPY on 3/6 for a −$29 realized loss when 680 support broke decisively (4 of 5 closes below). META still held, 1 share −3.4%, inside its −4% hard stop at 641.02. The exit discipline worked; the entry discipline didn't — specifically, adding to SPY on a *reclaim* of 680 rather than a *breakout* of 693 was buying inside a range that then resolved lower, and initiating META the same day doubled correlated risk. Playbook now requires range *breaks* for adds (not bounces), one new risk add per day across the book, regime-aware sizing (5–7% starters in chop, 8–10% only in confirmed trend), and written/resting stops rather than mental ones. Cash 93.5% into Monday, defensive bias, only re-engaging SPY on a 680 reclaim with volume or a 659–665 capitulation reversal; META exits at open if it gaps under 641. Watchlist gaining IWM, SMH, TLT, XLF, and a working VIX feed; dropping TSLA for inactivity.

**Week 3 summary for operator:** Closed −$0.74 / −0.01% on $9,948 — a functionally flat week in a tape that broke down hard (SPY 678→662, QQQ 608→594, fresh range lows on heavy volume). Three fills: SPY capitulation-reversal starter 3/9 @ 678.27, META time-stop 3/11 @ 654.86 (−$12.87), SPY close-breakdown exit 3/12 @ 666.06 (−$10.74). Net realized −$23.61, but META's mark-to-market recovered ~$10 from the prior week's unrealized hole, leaving the week flat. Two of three exits were the *sharpened-from-last-week* close-breakdown rule firing exactly as designed — that discipline saved real capital. The miss was the SPY 3/9 entry: a single-day capitulation reversal got starter-size instead of scout-size, and I held it three days without the required Day-2 close >680 confirmation. Playbook updates: capitulation reversals are now scout-only (3–5%) until Day-2 confirmation; every ticket needs a written Day-2 weakness criterion alongside the hard stop; in confirmed TREND-DOWN the active trade is defensive ETFs (TLT/GLD/SHY), not 100% cash. Watchlist adds: TLT, GLD, SHY/BIL, VIXY (3-week VIX feed miss — fix Monday), XLF. Drop: TSLA. Book is 100% cash going into Monday with a defensive bias; no new single-stock longs until SPY reclaims 670 with volume or flushes to 650–659 with multi-day reversal.

## Week 4 Summary for Operator

**Closed flat at $0.00 / 0.00% on $9,947.40, 100% cash, zero fills.** SPY fell 662 → 648 (−2.1%) on the week with fresh range lows Friday on the heaviest volume of the month (163M, close near LoD). Doing nothing was the trade — the mandate of "flat beats red" was met cleanly in a TREND-DOWN tape that offered only bear traps. Three correct passes: didn't chase the 3/17 weak bounce to 670.79 (volume failed the "regime flip" test), didn't scout the marginal 3/19 capitulation candle (Thu-into-Fri made Day-2 confirmation impossible), and didn't manufacture a setup just because four weeks had passed. The two open process bugs are now in stark relief: the VIX feed is unresolved for a fourth straight week (Monday tick-1 priority is to batch-test `VXX/UVXY/^VIX9D/^VVIX` until one returns data), and last week's "defensive ETFs are the active trade in TREND-DOWN" rule fell apart because TLT/GLD/SHY/VIXY all return empty in this harness — playbook now caveats that rule with "if and only if data exists; otherwise cash is the defensive position." Watchlist pruned: dropping AAPL/MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN/AMD from active monitoring (zero analytical attention in 3+ weeks); keeping SPY/QQQ/IWM/SMH/NVDA/META active. Monday trigger ladder: SPY >665 reclaim is a "bounce-alive" check (not entry), 630-640 flush with upper-half close on >110M vol = 3-5% scout, otherwise hold 100% cash.

**Week 5 summary for operator:** Closed flat at **$0.00 / 0.00%** on $9,947.40, 100% cash, zero fills — third flat week out of five, second consecutive in TREND-DOWN. SPY fell 648 → 634 (−2.2%) with a failed bounce 3/23-3/25 topping at 656 (well below the 665 reclaim trigger) and a fresh weekly low Friday at the close on 103M volume. The three correct passes were: (1) closing the 4-week-old defensive-ticker availability bug on Monday tick 1 by batch-testing every plausible vol/bond/gold/alt proxy — all empty, so cash is officially the only defensive expression and that rule is now baked in; (2) reading 3/23's gap-up-and-fade as distribution (heavy vol + lower-half close), not reversal, and watching Day-2 confirm the bearish read; (3) refusing to "round down" Friday's capitulation criteria when SPY tagged the trigger zone but closed at LoD on insufficient volume. The misses were process: I re-tested empty tickers 4 separate ticks after Monday's conclusive answer (wasted budget), did zero level-prep on the names I'd actually buy when regime flips (slow reaction loop), and never explicitly flagged the watchlist prune as an operator action. Playbook now mandates a weekly Level Prep Tick Tue/Wed on the active watchlist, codifies symmetric Day-2 invalidation for scouts, and retires both the VIX feed agenda and the "defensive ETF" rule for good. **Operator ask: please remove AAPL/MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN/TSLA/AMD from the active watchlist** — three weeks of zero analytical attention. Monday triggers: SPY >665 close on >90M vol = bounce-alive check; flush to 615-625 with upper-half close on >110M vol = 3-5% scout; otherwise 100% cash.

**Week 6 summary for operator:** Closed **+$15.59 / +0.16%** on $9,962.99 — the first green week in six, modest but on the right side of the mandate. Two fills, both buys, both in SPY: a 3.3% capitulation-reversal scout on 3/31 @ $650.34 after a clean 2-day V at the 629-640 support zone on 152M volume, and a 2.1% add on 4/8 @ $676.01 when SPY gapped and broke out of a 5-day 655-660 base on 93M volume with QQQ confirming. The position closed Friday at $679.46, +2.95% unrealized, with a BE stop active. The regime flip TREND-DOWN → early TREND-UP printed as the textbook 3-step sequence (capitulation candle + base + breakout-on-volume) my playbook describes, and the scout discipline (pattern over strict trigger spec, no add on weak base volume, written invalidation on every ticket) held cleanly. The honest miss was sizing — playbook says 8-10% starter in TREND-UP and I only got to 5.4%, leaving setup-quality return on the table — and zero diversification despite QQQ visibly leading; that's where Monday's plan focuses. Process gap repeating: the mandatory Tuesday Level Prep Tick still hasn't been executed, so QQQ/SMH/IWM/NVDA/META levels are stale. Playbook now adds an explicit single-position-concentration warning in TREND-UP and softens the strict gap-down filter for capitulation triggers. **Operator ask (3rd week running):** please swap AAPL/MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN/TSLA/AMD off the active watchlist for **IWM and SMH** — those are the actual rotation candidates now.

## Operator summary — Week 7 (2026-04-13 → 2026-04-17)

Closed **+$24.54 / +0.25%** on $9,987.53, second consecutive green week, lifetime now −0.12% (essentially scratch from the −0.53% hole three weeks ago). Zero fills — the entire week's gain came from holding the 3/31+4/8 SPY scout (0.8 sh @ 659.97) through a 5-day vertical melt-up (SPY 679 → 710, +4.5%; QQQ +6.2%; NVDA/META parabolic), advancing the trail stop with each new high while never panic-trimming. Three correct passes: held the winner, refused to chase the 4/13 light-vol HOD close, refused to chase the 4/16 Day-4 parabolic into Friday. The big miss is the same one as last week — book is still a single 5.7% SPY position in a confirmed TREND-UP where QQQ and tech leaders ran without me; the soft "concentration warning" got documented and ignored a second time. Playbook now converts that warning into a mechanical forcing rule (N=1 in TREND-UP for >1 tick = mandatory leader scout or written veto), adds an explicit "Day-2 of regime flip = scout leader at open" branch so vertical tapes that never offer pullbacks still get participation, and requires every Level Prep Tick to terminate in action/trigger/veto per name rather than bare level documentation. Monday is Day-5+ of vertical; new full-size adds are suspended until the first red day. **Operator ask (fourth week running):** please swap AAPL/MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN/TSLA/AMD off the active watchlist for IWM and SMH.

**Week 8 summary (2026-04-20 → 2026-04-24):** Closed **+$7.43 / +0.07%** on $9,994.96, third consecutive green week, lifetime now flat at −0.05%. One fill — the QQQ 0.5sh @ 655.11 leader scout on 4/22 that finally converted the concentration forcing rule from a documented two-week miss into a real position via Tuesday's pre-written trigger (QQQ test 642 hold + upper-half reversal close). SPY 0.8sh held cleanly through Thursday's outside-day-down (HH+lower close = mixed, not strict NEG-NEG → hold), then printed fresh ATH 713.94 Friday with QQQ confirming breakout to 663.88. Three correct passes: executed the concentration rule via paired trigger, terminated Tuesday Level Prep in per-name action/trigger/veto (process loop closed end-to-end for the first time), and read Thursday's pullback structurally instead of trimming. The honest miss is the same one that's run for three weeks now — gross book exposure is only **9%** in a confirmed TREND-UP week 3 while the tape did +0.7% SPY / +2.6% QQQ this week; the concentration rule moved me from N=1 to N=2 but didn't size me up. Playbook now adds an explicit **gross-exposure floor by regime** (TREND-UP ≥30%, target 50-70%) as a mechanical forcing rule, retires the fixed "scout = 3-5%" sizing in favor of setup-quality sizing (confirmed regime + clean trigger = 6-8% starter), and codifies strict NEG-NEG for Day-2 scout exits plus structure-band reading for "upper/lower half" trigger language. Monday 4/27 enters with a live forcing condition: gross floor breach must resolve into a leader add or written veto. **Operator standing ask (5th week):** please swap AAPL/MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN/TSLA/AMD off the active watchlist for IWM and SMH.

**Week 9 close 2026-05-01: +$43.16 / +0.43% on $10,038.12. Fourth consecutive green week; lifetime now positive +0.38% (first time above water).** Two positions: SPY 2.13sh @ 693.59 (+3.9%), QQQ 2.55sh @ 661.17 (+2.0%); gross 32.4% at the TREND-UP floor; cash 67.6%. The week's win was mechanical: the new gross-exposure-floor forcing rule from last week's playbook actually fired — Mon SPY starter, Tue QQQ trigger prep, Wed-Thu paired tranches on shakeout reversal and 3-day-base breakout — and rebuilt gross from 9% to 32% in four sessions while the tape printed fresh ATHs on both SPY (724.87) and QQQ. Setup-quality sizing (5-7% tranches, not reflexive 3% scouts) added real dollars vs. the prior weeks' under-sizing. Two honest misses: (1) Wednesday took two correlated adds in one tick, technically breaking "one risk add per day" — playbook now permits same-day correlated tranches under live floor-breach with size/concentration guardrails; (2) zero single-name diversification for a fifth week despite NVDA/META/AMD all running on the actual watchlist, so the new rule is "stop waiting on operator watchlist updates, trade what's available." Friday closed lower-quartile on lighter vol at ATH — first distribution whiff — so Monday plan includes a written trim trigger if SPY can't reclaim 720 midday. Standing operator ask (6th week): IWM/SMH on the active watchlist would help diversification, but I'll stop blocking on it.

**Week 10 close 2026-05-08: +$139.56 / +1.39% on $10,177.68.** Fifth consecutive green week, lifetime now **+1.78%** — best week and highest lifetime mark since onboarding. Three positions all green: SPY 1.83sh +6.35%/+$80.57, QQQ 2.55sh +7.57%/+$127.65, NVDA 2sh +3.55%/+$14.74; gross 35.3% above the 30% TREND-UP floor with room to ~50%. The week's real wins were process: the Fri-written Mon-trim protocol fired exactly as scripted (locked $7 on the SPY add tranche before Tue's ATH rip), the 6-week-old single-name concentration finally broke via a textbook NVDA capitulation→base→breakout entry on 188M-vol gap day, and Thu's lower-third close got correctly read as digestion (not distribution) rather than triggering a reflexive trim. The honest misses are sizing and reconciliation: NVDA went in at 4% when the new setup-quality rule says 6-8% for confirmed-regime + clean-trigger + watchlist-prepped names (under-sized for the third week running), and the GOOGL trigger written into Tuesday's level prep never got checked Wednesday because NVDA's setup was easier to act on. Playbook now adds a forcing test on size defaults, a mandatory Wed trigger-reconciliation step before new ideas, same-tick trail-ladder advancement instead of Friday batch, and retires the mood-based "yellow flag" labeling in favor of strict distribution criteria (heavy vol AND lower-half close). Monday's plan: NVDA Day-3 confirmation upsize is mandatory per the size rule, GOOGL/META base setups get Tue level prep, and no chasing the vertical QQQ at +7.57%.

**Week 11 operator summary (2026-05-11 → 2026-05-15):** Closed **+$17.27 / +0.17%** on $10,194.95 — sixth consecutive green week, lifetime now +1.95% (new high), but the thinnest green of the streak after Friday gave back nearly all of Thursday's ATH push. Three fills, all buys: NVDA upsize 1.5sh @ 219.44 Mon executing last week's setup-quality rule cleanly (no timidity, 7.5% size on Day-3 confirmation), and GOOGL starter 1.5sh @ 402.62 Wed firing exactly through the Tue-write/Wed-reconcile process loop that closed two weeks ago's bug. Same-tick trail-ladder advancement ran four sessions clean (SPY/QQQ/NVDA all ratcheting through +3/+6/+10 crossings as they printed) — no Friday-batch panic. Three honest misses: GOOGL entry was a HoD chase on an extended breakout bar (currently -1.45%, would have been ~2% better via a base-retest limit), no same-day trim on Friday's QQQ strict-distribution + NVDA outside-reversal (deferred to Mon when same-day partial-trim was warranted), and gross exposure peaked at only 45% in TREND-UP wk6 when the target is 50%+. Playbook gains three new rules: (1) breakout-entry tactic — extended-bar breakouts get a Day-2 limit at base-edge+0.5%, not market at HoD; (2) Friday strict-distribution at vertical ATH wk5+ with position +6% permits same-day partial trim (the blanket "no Fri initiations" rule retired and replaced with "no Fri adds, trims permitted on defined warrants"); (3) gross-exposure *target* forcing rule pushing +5-7% per week toward 50% in confirmed TREND-UP wk4+ with no distribution. Vertical Day-5+ trails tighten to -3%. Monday's pre-committed trigger ladder is loaded: NVDA Day-2 NEG-NEG check, QQQ noon-reclaim test, GOOGL invalidation watch, no new initiations until Tue.

**Week 12 summary for operator (2026-05-18 → 2026-05-22):** Closed **−$11.40 / −0.11%** on $10,183.55 — the first red week in seven, but only just, and structurally one realized loss (GOOGL −$29.47 on Fri hard-stop exit from a bad entry last week) absorbed almost entirely by SPY/QQQ mark-up (+$95 / +$144). Lifetime now +1.84%, off the +1.95% prior-week high. Two fills, both sells: NVDA Day-2 strict NEG-NEG trim Mon 5/18 @ 222.32 (1.5sh, pre-committed trigger fired clean), and GOOGL full exit Fri 5/22 @ 382.97 on −4.88% hard-stop + 385 invalidation break. The week's process wins were three: the Fri-write/Mon-execute loop closed cleanly for a third consecutive week (NVDA trim), QQQ's Tue 5/19 intraday trail breach (low 695.25 vs −3% trail @ 698) was held through correctly on the close-stop rule and the position recovered +2.3%, and Fri's GOOGL exit followed the rule book on a busted entry with no debate about weekend gap risk. The honest miss was under-deployment Wed-Thu: SPY printed clean 740+ ATH reclaim days post-Tue distribution and I held cash 59% — the 0.3sh SPY tranche I had trimmed 5/4 should have been re-added on the reclaim, but I didn't have a pre-written re-add trigger. Playbook now adds: (1) **trimmed-tranche re-add ≠ new initiation**, pre-write the re-add trigger at time of trim, (2) **intraday-trail-breach with close-back-above** = hold + Day-2 watch + tighten next ratchet by 1% (resolves the close-vs-intraday ambiguity), (3) **hard stops execute Fri same-day, no exception**, and retires the standalone gross-push +5-7%/wk rule in favor of a conditional version requiring 5+ distribution-free sessions AND a clean base-retest entry available (prevents the GOOGL-style chase-bar pressure). Monday loads with NVDA Day-2 NEG-NEG check, an SPY re-add trigger >743, and no new single-name initiations until Tue level prep.

**Week 13 operator summary (2026-05-26 short week):** Closed **+$40.60 / +0.40%** on $10,224.15 — green week resumed immediately after wk12's −$11.40 break, lifetime now **+2.24% (new high)**. One fill: NVDA full exit 2sh @ 214.86 Tue post-holiday on strict Day-2 NEG-NEG vs Fri 5/22 (H 218.18<221.01 AND C 214.86<215.33), pre-committed trigger firing clean for the 4th consecutive week (promoted to standard process). SPY and QQQ both ramped to fresh ATHs every session — SPY 745.64→750.59 (+0.66%), QQQ 717.54→730.28 (+1.78%) — driving combined unrealized to +$280; QQQ crossed +10% so trail advanced same-tick to −8% @ 672.68. Three correct passes: NEG-NEG exit on schedule, held SPY/QQQ through last Fri's distribution into this week's ATH ramp (rule said hold, rule was right), and honored the strict vol gate on the SPY tiered re-add when Tue's 40.96M vol failed 47M 20d avg. The honest miss is the same one for the third week running — the 0.3sh SPY trim from 5/4 has now cost ~$10 of foregone restoration while the strict price+vol gate stays unfired in a vertical-extension regime where vol naturally compresses. Playbook now adds **tiered tranche re-add** (price-only = 50% size, price+vol = 100%), a **vertical-extension exception** for the gross-push conditional (tiered re-adds count as deployable when no base-retest entry exists), and an **ATR%-conditional sizing gate** (>2.5% ATR = starter-only, no upsize tranches — NVDA's 3-week campaign netted only +$18 because mechanical triggers exit at the noise floor on volatile names). Standing operator ask (8th week): IWM/SMH on active watchlist would help diversification.
